first.rationale: Targeted promotional pricing most directly addresses current SMB losses and previously produced strong acquisition and revenue lift. Verify its downstream retention and qualified-revenue durability, while checking shortened onboarding as the strongest sustainable alternative given declining completion and activation.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening onboarding. The verified source shows higher completion, faster time-to-value, and improved 30-day retention, directly addressing both current onboarding and activation declines while supporting sustainable revenue. Reject promotional pricing this cycle because its verified 12% retention decline undermines long-term qualified revenue despite near-term gains.

final2.rationale: Proceed with shortened onboarding. Its verified record improved completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention, directly supporting sustainable qualified revenue. The competitor escalation increases urgency but does not reverse the verified evidence that a 40% SMB discount reduced 30-day retention by 12%; promotional pricing is therefore unsuitable without a safer, newly verified design. The current price-driven churn signal remains a risk and should be reassessed when verification capacity resets.
